profile.founded_lineage: Formed through merger of two predecessor colocation companies: ViaWest (founded 1999, Western US) and Peak 10 (founded 2000, Southeastern US); Peak 10 acquired ViaWest in 2017 and the combined company rebranded as Flexential in 2018

reading:
Flexential is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, and formed from the 2017 merger of two predecessor colocation companies, Peak 10, founded in 2000 to serve the Southeastern US, and ViaWest, founded in 1999 to serve the Western US. The combined company took the Flexential name in 2018 after also acquiring AppliedTrust and INetU in 2015 to expand its professional services and cloud portfolio.

The company is privately held, GI Partners is its controlling sponsor per Flexential's own announcement of a GI Partners continuation vehicle and a GI Data Infrastructure strategic investment, and North Carolina business press separately reports Flexential received a strategic investment from a Morgan Stanley infrastructure unit. Flexential's site states the company secured $2.1 billion in financing in 2021 for growth and sustainability initiatives, and describes its footprint only in round terms, more than 40 data centers across 18 national markets, with more than 800 employees and 3,000 customers across more than 20 industries, without a precise facility count, megawatt capacity figure, or per-market investment breakdown.

The registry here tracks 43 Flexential facilities across fifteen states, Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Minnesota, North Carolina, Nevada, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, and Virginia, a wide multi-region colocation footprint consistent with the ViaWest and Peak 10 predecessor geographies it was built from, Western states from ViaWest, Southeastern states from Peak 10.
